data.text: PMID 42961571: "Genomic signatures of HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma and its precursor lesions." (Indian J Pathol Microbiol, 2026). Abstract: Genomic signatures of HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma and its precursor lesions.. Early diagnosis of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) and its precursors is still a challenge to overcome. So far, research on the genomic characterization of VSCC tumors has been limited. We retrospectively analyzed mutational data, histology, and clinical features of eight samples from six patients (including four HPV-negative VSCC patients with adjacent differentiated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (dVIN) tissues, one vulvar lichen sclerosus patient, and one vulvar acanthosis with altered differentiation-like patient). Targeted deep sequencing was performed on these samples with adjacent normal tissues as controls. Only one VSCC patient had moderately/poorly differentiated carcinoma, and neither TP53 nor PIK3CA mutations were identified in this case. Among the remaining seven samples, TERT (7/7) was the most frequently mutated gene, followed by TP53 ( 4/7), CASP8 ( 4/7), and NOTCH1

data.text: PMID 42951252: "Invasive Lobular Carcinoma With Extracellular Mucin Production: First Whole Exome Sequencing of a Rare Histological Variant of Breast Carcinoma." (Mod Pathol, 2026). Abstract: Invasive Lobular Carcinoma With Extracellular Mucin Production: First Whole Exome Sequencing of a Rare Histological Variant of Breast Carcinoma.. Invasive lobular carcinoma with extracellular mucin production (ILCEMP) is a rare histological variant of invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), with only about 40 cases described in the English literature. In the latest WHO classification of breast tumours, ILCEMP is described under the mucinous carcinoma section, noting that it is not certain whether these tumours represent a subtype of ILC or mucinous carcinoma. We performed whole-exome sequencing in seven ILCEMP primary tumors and two matched regional metastatic lymph nodes from seven patients. Samples were provided by six different European institutions. Most cases have been previously described histologically in two studies. data.text: PMID 42621186: "Identification of novel UBE2E3::PDE1A and CTC1::MEF2C fusion transcripts in acute myeloid leukemia." (Ther Adv Hematol, 2026). Abstract: Identification of novel. Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a hematologic malignancy caused by the malignant proliferation and differentiation block of immature myeloid cells (blasts) in the bone marrow. The pathogenesis, diagnostic classification, treatment, and prognosis of AML are fundamentally linked to the accumulation of genetic variants, fusion gene formation, and chromosomal karyotype abnormalities. Using mRNA sequencing (next-generation sequencing, NGS), we identified and validated two novel fusion genes, UBE2E3::PDE1A and CTC1::MEF2C, in a case of AML-M2a. This patient also harbored six single nucleotide variants (SNV) (EP300, KRAS, NRAS, RAD21, TET2, and TP53) and complex karyotype (CK). The chromosomes exhibited extreme instability and high variability, with tumor cells containing multiple clones and showing continuous karyotype evolution as the disease progressed. data.title: Grounded Interpretation
data.content:
The variant rs28934578 in TP53 is classified as Likely pathogenic by ClinVar. It is associated with drug responses to platinum compounds and antineoplastic agents, with increased risk of neutropenia in certain genotypes. Limited evidence suggests it may be involved in various cancers, including vulvar squamous cell carcinoma and invasive lobular carcinoma with extracellular mucin production.

**Limitations:**
- Ensembl could not be reached; this report is partial.
- Ensembl variant effect prediction was unavailable due to unreachability of the Ensembl server.
- Limited clinical evidence is available for the specific variant rs28934578 in TP53.
